Natural Resources Canada, Canadian Industry Program for Energy Conservation (CIPEC), in collaboration with the Pulp and Paper Research Institute of Canada (Paprican) (2008). Benchmarking Energy Use in Canadian Pulp and Paper Mills. Office of Energy Efficiency, Ottawa. ISBN 0-662-69589-5, Cat. No. M144-121/2006 (catalogued 2006, copyright 2008). No individual authors named.

Paprican area-by-area energy benchmarking of 49 Canadian mills (51 surveyed, 55% of Canadian capacity; survey years not printed, quarterly data for four quarters). Loaded: every area of Tables 3-3 to 3-19 as median (value) with 25th and 75th percentiles (value-min/value-max) in one process context, and the "Modern" literature values as separate examples in a second context; product routes (Tables 4-1 to 4-4) likewise. Units kept as printed: pulp areas per oven-dry tonne (ODt), product and common areas per air-dry tonne (ADt), boilers per GJ thermal produced, turbines MJ/kWh. Thermal energy = steam consumed minus condensate returned (not fuel). Boiler efficiency derived as 100/(GJ fuel per GJ thermal) with formula. Not loaded: Figures 3-1 to 4-5 (per-mill bars, no printed values), Appendix B (hypothetical sample mill), deaerator % and data-quality stats (other-values). Locator: printed page numbers (report pp.1-56). Traps: some evaporator electricity was metered in the recovery boiler area (evaporator electricity low, recovery boiler high); Table 4-4 "net thermal energy production" column appears to be net consumption; ODt vs ADt bases must not be mixed; Table 4-x fuel includes black liquor. No costs.
